answers.explanation: Referencing SecureString parameters in environment variables exposes secrets and does not ensure automatic secret updates without redeployment.

questions.content:
A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application
needs to use dynamic feature flags that will be shared with other applications.
The application must poll on an interval for new feature flag values. The values
must be cached when they are retrieved.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient
way?

answers.content: Store the feature flag values in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure an Amazon ElastiCache node to cache the values by using a lazy loading strategy in the application. Update the application to poll for the values on an interval from ElastiCache.
answers.explanation: Secrets Manager is primarily for secret management, not dynamic configuration, and adding ElastiCache for caching adds operational complexity.

answers.content: Store the feature flag values in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache the values by using a lazy loading strategy in the application. Update the application to poll for the values on an interval from DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB with DAX is possible but involves more overhead and complexity compared to using a dedicated configuration service like AppConfig.

answers.content: Store the feature flag values in AWS AppConfig. Configure AWS AppConfig Agent on the EC2 instances to poll for the values on an interval. Update the application to retrieve the values from the AppConfig Agent localhost endpoint.
answers.explanation: AWS AppConfig is designed specifically for managing dynamic configuration data including feature flags. AWS AppConfig Agent on EC2 instances supports polling at configured intervals, complying with the requirement for polling and caching feature flags locally. AppConfig provides built-in mechanisms to manage feature flag updates efficiently and securely without custom caching layers, improving operational efficiency. This solution uses a managed service designed for configuration deployment which is more operationally efficient than custom caching or polling from Secrets Manager, DynamoDB, or Parameter Store.

answers.content: Store the feature flag values in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to poll on an interval. Configure the application to use the AWS SDK to retrieve the values from Parameter Store and to store the values in memory.
answers.explanation: Using Parameter Store requires manual polling and caching in the application, increasing operational complexity and potential for stale data.

questions.content:
A company uses two AWS accounts: production and development. The company stores
data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is in the production account. The data is
encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The
company plans to copy the data to another S3 bucket that is in the development
account.

A developer needs to use a KMS key to encrypt the data in the S3 bucket that is
in the development account. The KMS key in the development account must be
accessible from the production account,

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Replicate the customer managed KMS key from the production account to the development account. Specify the production account in the key policy.
answers.explanation: Customer managed KMS keys cannot be replicated between accounts; each key must be created and managed independently.

answers.content: Create a new customer managed KMS key in the development account. Specify the production account in the key policy.
answers.explanation: Creating a new customer managed KMS key in the development account and specifying the production account in the key policy allows controlled cross-account access to the key. Customer managed keys provide full control over key usage and policies, which aligns with the need for explicit access from the production account. This approach follows security best practices by not sharing or replicating keys but rather granting precise access through key policies.

answers.content: Create a new AWS managed KMS key for Amazon S3 in the development account. Specify the production account in the key policy.
answers.explanation: AWS managed keys do not allow specifying custom key policies, including granting access to other accounts.

answers.content: Replicate the default AWS managed KMS key for Amazon S3 from the production account to the development account. Specify the production account in the key policy.
answers.explanation: Default AWS managed keys cannot be replicated across accounts, and custom policies cannot be applied to them.

questions.content:
A company has an AWS Step Functions state machine named myStateMachine. The
company configured a service role for Step Functions.

The developer must ensure that only the myStateMachine state machine can assume
the service role.

Which statement should the developer add to the trust policy to meet this
requirement?

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image39.png]
answers.explanation: Allows any Step Functions state machine to assume the role without restriction to myStateMachine.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image40.png]
answers.explanation: Uses 'sts:SourceAccount' which restricts by account but not to the specific state machine, so broader than required.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image41.png]
answers.explanation: The trust policy must specify that only the specific Step Functions state machine (myStateMachine) can assume the role. Using the 'sts:SourceArn' condition with the full ARN of myStateMachine restricts the assume role permission to that particular state machine. This approach follows AWS best practices by tightly scoping trust relationships for enhanced security. Options involving 'sts:SourceAccount' or omitting a SourceArn condition allow broader access, which is less secure.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image42.png]
answers.explanation: References 'Principal' as the state machine ARN directly, which is not valid for IAM trust policies; Principal must be a service or AWS entity.

questions.content:
A developer is designing an event-driven architecture. An AWS Lambda function
that processes data needs to push processed data to a subset of four consumer
Lambda functions. The data must be routed based on the value of one field in the
data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and event source mapping for each consumer Lambda function. Add message routing logic to the data-processing Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Using SQS queues with event source mapping requires additional routing logic in the producer Lambda and managing multiple queues, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the four consumer Lambda functions to the topic. Add message filtering logic to each consumer Lambda function. Subscribe the data-processing Lambda function to the SNS topic.
answers.explanation: Adding message filtering logic within each consumer Lambda is less efficient and adds operational complexity.

answers.content: Create a separate Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and subscription for each consumer Lambda function. Add message routing logic to the data-processing Lambda function to publish to the appropriate topic.
answers.explanation: Creating separate SNS topics and subscriptions per consumer increases management overhead compared to using a single topic with filter policies.

answers.content: Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the four consumer Lambda functions to the topic. Add SNS subscription filter policies to each subscription. Configure the data-processing Lambda function to publish to the topic.
answers.explanation: Using a single SNS topic with subscription filter policies allows routing based on message attributes without requiring additional routing logic in the producer Lambda function. SNS subscription filter policies enable simple and efficient message filtering per consumer Lambda, reducing operational overhead. Managed service SNS with filter policies is preferred over custom routing logic or multiple topics for routing to subsets of consumers.

questions.content:
A developer is building an application that stores sensitive user data. The
application includes an Amazon CloudFront distribution and multiple AWS Lambda
functions that handle user requests.

The user requests contain over 20 data fields. Each application transaction
contains sensitive data that must be encrypted. Only specific parts of the
application need to have the ability to decrypt the data.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Associate the CloudFront distribution with a Lambda@Edge function. Configure the function to perform field-level asymmetric encryption by using a user-defined RSA public key that is stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
answers.explanation: Lambda@Edge cannot perform field-level asymmetric encryption using KMS keys directly; implementing encryption in Lambda@Edge is custom and not managed.

answers.content: Integrate AWS WAF with CloudFront to protect the sensitive data. Use a Lambda function and self-managed keys to perform the encryption and decryption processes.
answers.explanation: Using self-managed keys and Lambda for encryption/decryption is less secure and not a managed AWS solution, violating best practices.

answers.content: Configure the CloudFront distribution to use WebSockets by forwarding all viewer request headers to the origin. Create an asymmetric AWS KMS key. Configure the CloudFront distribution to use field-level encryption. Use the AWS KMS key.
answers.explanation: CloudFront supports field-level encryption, which can encrypt specific data fields in user requests. Using AWS KMS asymmetric keys for field-level encryption ensures secure encryption and decryption of sensitive data. Field-level encryption allows only designated parts of the application to decrypt sensitive fields, aligning with the requirement that only specific parts have decryption ability. Configuring CloudFront to use field-level encryption with AWS KMS managed keys leverages a managed service designed for security, avoiding custom key management solutions.

answers.content: Configure the cache behavior in the CloudFront distribution to require HTTPS for communication between viewers and CloudFront. Configure GoudFront to require users to access the files by using either signed URLs or signed cookies.
answers.explanation: Requiring HTTPS and signed URLs/cookies secures transport and access but does not address required encryption of sensitive data fields or field-level encryption.

questions.content:
A developer built an application that uses AWS Lambda functions to process
images. The developer wants to improve image processing times throughout the
day.

The developer needs to create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights query that
shows the average, slowest, and fastest processing time in 1-minute intervals.

Which query will meet these requirements?

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image23.png]
answers.explanation: Does not aggregate using avg, max, and min correctly or uses incorrect syntax for 1-minute intervals.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image24.png]
answers.explanation: Option B uses stats avg(processingTime) as avg, max(processingTime) as slowest, and min(processingTime) as fastest to compute average, slowest, and fastest processing times respectively. It groups the results by bin(1m) to show data in 1-minute intervals, meeting the requirement exactly. This aligns with best practices for CloudWatch Logs Insights queries for statistical aggregation over time bins.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image25.png]
answers.explanation: Likely uses incorrect aggregation functions or lacks grouping by 1-minute intervals.

answers.content: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image26.png]
answers.explanation: Does not compute all three required metrics or uses incorrect query structure.
